standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic weighing tradeoffs explicitly task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario (a teen choosing between two realistic part-time commitments that conflict, such as a weekend job offer versus a sports commitment already made) and works through it using a tradeoff table.
safetyNotes: The scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to disclose or decide about any real personal commitment of their own.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Did the tradeoff table change your answer from your warm-up instinct? If it stayed the same, what changed about how confident you are and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options. | Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning. | Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner rewrite the scenario with a third option added (a compromise or a delayed decision) and redo the tradeoff table with all three options.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic weighing tradeoffs explicitly task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario (a teen choosing between two realistic part-time commitments that conflict, such as a weekend job offer versus a sports commitment already made) and works through it using a tradeoff table.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact weighing tradeoffs explicitly decision or action.
Model move 2: Before comparing options, write down your first instinct for what the character should choose.
Model move 3: Build a tradeoff table comparing both options on the same three criteria: money/commitment, time, and what is given up.

Model check: Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options. | Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning. | Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for weighing tradeoffs explicitly.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario (a teen choosing between two realistic part-time commitments that conflict, such as a weekend job offer versus a sports commitment already made) and works through it using a tradeoff table.
Coach direction: Before comparing options, write down your first instinct for what the character should choose.
Learner prompt: What is your gut-instinct answer for what the character should do, before working through the tradeoffs?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build a tradeoff table comparing both options on the same three criteria: money/commitment, time, and what is given up.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I filled in both options for the money/commitment criterion.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I filled in both options for the time criterion.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I filled in both options for the 'what is given up' criterion.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Did the tradeoff table change your answer from your warm-up instinct? If it stayed the same, what changed about how confident you are and why?

Success checks: Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options. | Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning. | Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional weighing tradeoffs explicitly condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options. | Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning. | Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: weighing tradeoffs explicitly — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the weighing tradeoffs explicitly task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Did the tradeoff table change your answer from your warm-up instinct? If it stayed the same, what changed about how confident you are and why?
observableCriteria: Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options.
Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning.
Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Table completeness and balance: All three criteria are filled in honestly for both options. | Justification grounded in the table: Recommendation cites at least two specific rows from the table as reasoning. | Reflective comparison: Reflection states whether the answer changed and gives a reason.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
